question: What is the main focus of a community diagnosis?

options.A: The health status of an entire population
options.B: The medical history of individual clinic staff
options.C: The recovery rate of a single hospital patient
options.D: The financial budget of a local health clinic

explanation: Spot on! Unlike individual care where you treat one patient at a time, a community diagnosis looks at the overall health picture of an entire group of people. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h1)

question: Why do nurses conduct a community diagnosis before launching a new health program?

options.A: It guarantees that funding from international donors will be approved
options.B: It helps identify the root causes and main health problems of the population
options.C: It allows nurses to avoid interacting directly with community leaders
options.D: It replaces the need for individual patient medical records completely

explanation: You got it! Checking the community first makes sure our interventions actually solve the real problems facing the people there. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h1)

question: What is one key reason for conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To allocate scarce health resources where they are needed most
options.B: To increase the patient population inside large urban hospitals
options.C: To eliminate the need for community health workers in rural areas
options.D: To reduce the salaries of local public health administrators

explanation: Exactly! Since resources like funding and medical supplies are often limited, a community diagnosis helps us direct them to the areas that need them most. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h2)

question: How does involving local residents in a community diagnosis help public health programs?

options.A: It builds local ownership and cooperation for the health programs
options.B: It shifts all financial responsibility entirely onto the villagers
options.C: It ensures that no diseases will ever reappear in the community
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to collect any data themselves

explanation: Spot on! When community members are part of identifying their challenges, they are much more willing to embrace and support the solutions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h2)

question: What do we call a community diagnosis that zeroes in on one specific health issue or vulnerable group?
explanation: Well done! A problem-oriented assessment focuses tightly on a particular issue or group rather than trying to examine everything at once. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h3)

question: A team of student nurses investigates a sudden outbreak of measles in a single village. What kind of diagnosis are they doing?
explanation: Correct! Because they are zeroing in on one specific outbreak (measles), this is a classic problem-oriented approach. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h3)

question: During which phase of a community diagnosis do nurses actually go out to collect field data?
explanation: You nailed it! The survey phase is the action time when nurses hit the field to gather data through interviews and observations. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h4)

question: What is the main focus during the pre-survey phase of a community diagnosis?

options.A: Analyzing raw data statistics using advanced computer software
options.B: Treating patients identified with severe malaria infections
options.C: Planning, setting objectives, and getting administrative approval
options.D: Presenting the final health report to village elders

explanation: Exactly right! The pre-survey phase is all about groundwork: planning, organizing, and securing permission before entering the community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h4)

question: Which of these is a great example of secondary data in a community assessment?

options.A: Focus group discussions with local market women
options.B: Direct visual observations of village water sources
options.C: Interviews conducted by nurses during home visits
options.D: Clinic registers and existing census reports

explanation: Spot on! Secondary data is information that was already collected by someone else and is sitting in existing records and reports. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h5)

question: A nurse wants to check birth and death rates in a district over the past five years. Where should she look first?

options.A: Interviews with children playing in the village square
options.B: Direct street observations during the afternoon rush
options.C: Existing government health records and vital statistics
options.D: A brand new questionnaire given to newborn babies

explanation: You got it! Birth and death records are historical government data, making them perfect secondary sources for vital statistics. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h5)

question: What is the main goal of analyzing data collected from a community?

options.A: To hide negative statistics from the local government
options.B: To increase the paperwork burden on student nurses
options.C: To identify concrete community health problems and trends
options.D: To replace the need for physical community visits

explanation: Correct! Data analysis helps turn raw numbers into clear patterns so we can see what health challenges the community is truly facing. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h6)

question: Why do nurses convert raw tally numbers into percentages and rates when analyzing data?

options.A: To make the final report look more complicated to read
options.B: To eliminate the need to collect any information from households
options.C: To make the health findings easier to interpret and compare
options.D: To prevent community members from understanding the results

explanation: Spot on! Percentages and rates give meaning to raw numbers, helping us clearly see the proportion of people affected by an issue. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h6)

question: When nurses are faced with multiple community health problems, which factor helps them decide which to tackle first?

options.A: Color of the local clinic building
options.B: Number of desks in the health office
options.C: Magnitude and severity of the problem
options.D: Personal preference of the junior nurse

explanation: Well done! Problems that affect a lot of people or cause severe illness naturally take top priority in our planning. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h7)

question: Why is priority setting such an important step in community health nursing?

options.A: Health laws prohibit nurses from tackling more than one disease
options.B: Most communities only ever experience a single health issue
options.C: It ensures that minor problems are always treated before major ones
options.D: Resources are never enough to solve every health problem at once

explanation: Exactly! Because time, money, and staff are always limited, we have to prioritize which issues need our immediate attention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring during a community health project?

options.A: Continuous tracking of activities to ensure they stay on schedule
options.B: Punishing staff members who arrive late to the clinic
options.C: Waiting until the very end of the project to check patient files
options.D: Increasing the financial budget halfway through the program

explanation: You got it! Monitoring happens while the project is running so we can catch delays or issues early and fix them. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h8)

question: How does evaluation differ from monitoring in a community health program?

options.A: Evaluation is optional, whereas monitoring is required by international law
options.B: Evaluation focuses entirely on staff discipline, while monitoring deals with drug supplies
options.C: Evaluation assesses the final outcomes and impact, while monitoring tracks ongoing daily activities
options.D: Evaluation is done before any data is collected, while monitoring happens only at the end

explanation: Spot on! Monitoring checks the process as it happens day-to-day, while evaluation measures the final results and overall success of the project. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h8)
